original_source_text: FPGAs are well-suited for dataflow architectures that process data in a streaming or pipelined manner, thus satisfying the high computational and communication demands of emerging applications. However, manually implementing an efficient dataflow architecture for large-scale applications is still challenging, even for specialists who use high-level synthesis (HLS) to simplify FPGA programming. To address this, we introduce CODO, an automated compiler that generates feasible and efficient dataflow accelerators on FPGAs. CODO features a systematic method for detecting and eliminating both coarse-grained and fine-grained dataflow violations. Building on this, CODO performs both on- and off-chip data movement optimizations to maximize transfer efficiency. To guarantee a higher design quality, CODO performs automatic scheduling to generate high-performance dataflow accelerators, ensuring a balanced performance-resource trade-off. Synthesis results show that CODO delivers $1.45\times$ to $4.52\times$ latency speedups on typical computation kernels and $3.7\times$ to $33.8\times$ speedups on DNN models compared to SOTA frameworks. In on-board evaluations, CODO achieves $7.3\times$ average speedup on CNN models and $2.07\times$ average speedup on the GPT-2 model over SOTA frameworks. The compiler is open-sourced at this https URL .

record_under_review.evidence_span: The paper presents an automated compiler for FPGA dataflow accelerators. It detects and removes coarse- and fine-grained dataflow violations, optimizes on-chip and off-chip data movement, and automatically schedules designs to balance performance and resource use. The reported results include 1.45x–4.52x latency speedups on computation kernels, 3.7x–33.8x speedups on DNN models, 7.3x average speedup on CNNs, and 2.07x speedup on GPT-2; the artifact is publicly released.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: FPGA dataflow accelerators and high-level-synthesis tool flows; the public evidence does not establish applicability to ASIC implementation or all FPGA families.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author arXiv preprint plus public artifact documentation; the repository has not independently reproduced synthesis or board results, extracted every baseline/configuration, or established generalization beyond the reported FPGA flows.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: CODO compiler built around systematic coarse- and fine-grained dataflow-violation detection and repair, on-chip/off-chip data-movement optimization, automatic scheduling, and a public artifact implementation.
metrics: 7.3x average CNN speedup in on-board evaluation
record_under_review.problem: Manual construction of efficient streaming FPGA dataflow accelerators remains difficult even with high-level synthesis because dataflow legality, communication efficiency, and resource/performance tradeoffs interact.
record_under_review.title: CODO: An Automated Compiler for Comprehensive Dataflow Optimization
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Typical computation kernels, DNN models, CNN models, and GPT-2 evaluated through synthesis and on-board FPGA experiments.
